why: PyTorch plan, 'Use the Mac GPU' (the model's parameters and each batch are on the same chosen device). The learner wrote xb.to(device) on its own line: a tensor's .to() returns a new tensor and leaves xb where it was, so the cell prints 'mps:0 cpu'. The model is on the GPU and the batch is still on the CPU; the next forward pass would fail with a device mismatch. Both device names are on screen and .to(device) is typed, but they are different devices, which is the one thing the step checks.

step.title: Put the model and a batch on the same device
step.instructions: In sine.ipynb, set device = torch.device('mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else 'cpu'). Move the model with model = model.to(device), take one batch from loader and move it with xb = xb.to(device), then show the device of the model's first parameter and of xb. Both must name the same device.

cells.source:
import torch
from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader

torch.manual_seed(0)
x0 = torch.linspace(-3.14, 3.14, 1000)
x1 = torch.rand(1000) * 4 - 2
X = torch.stack([x0, x1], dim=1)
y = (x1 > torch.sin(x0)).float().unsqueeze(1)
loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(X, y), batch_size=32, shuffle=True)

from torch import nn

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 1))
loss_fn = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss()
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)

device = torch.device('mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else 'cpu')
model = model.to(device)
xb, yb = next(iter(loader))
xb.to(device)
print(next(model.parameters()).device, xb.device)
